name: Vauxhall Vivaro Electric
summary: The UK's most common used electric mid-size van, sold in big numbers on fleet leases from 2020-21. It's a sensible used buy for local and regional work. Pick the 75kWh battery unless your daily miles are short and predictable.

generations.label: Vivaro-e (first version)

batteries.realWorldMiles: about 110 (EV Database estimates roughly 80-170 depending on temperature/road)
batteries.notes: Usable figure from EV Database (46.3kWh on the passenger Vivaro-e Life, same pack). Late-run vans are sometimes listed as '49kWh'.

batteries.realWorldMiles: about 150-160 (EV Database: 160 miles for Vivaro-e Life XL 75)
batteries.notes: Usable ~68kWh per GreenCarsCompare; owner forum puts it 'around 65'. EV Database average 10-80% DC rate ~77kW.

generations.notes: 100kW (136PS), 260Nm front motor on both batteries. DC 0-80%: about 32 min (50kWh), about 45-48 min (75kWh) at a 100kW charger (Parkers). AC: 7.4kW single-phase standard (Parkers); 11kW three-phase onboard charger optional (shown in adverts as '(11kW Charger)' or '[11kWCh]'; only helps on a three-phase supply). No battery preconditioning for rapid charging is documented, so winter DC speeds drop.

generations.label: Vivaro Electric (facelift)

batteries.notes: Parkers' March 2024 report on the facelift says the 50kWh and 75kWh choices both continued, so earlier sources saying the 50kWh was dropped look wrong. Parkers' price guide lists 50kWh vans in the later Prime trim, and 2025-registered 50kWh Vivaro Electrics are for sale on Parkers.

generations.notes: Facelift (new nose, revised steering, optional 10-inch screen with wireless phone connection, per Parkers). Same 136PS/260Nm motor quoted; improved battery tech/cooling gives the higher WLTP range. DC 5-80% about 45 min at 100kW. We found no source for a new motor on the medium vans.

batteryWarranty: 8 years / 100,000 miles on the battery (Parkers), to 70% capacity (Vauxhall listings). Standard vehicle warranty 3 years / 100,000 miles (Parkers). Parkers says a battery certification programme is meant to reassure used buyers. Transfer to a second owner isn't stated in the sources we found, but the cover runs from first registration, so a 2021 van still has it until 2029. Confirm with a Vauxhall dealer.

knownIssues.issue: Loss of drive / 'Electric traction system fault' warnings
knownIssues.detail: The 2022-23 builds had recalls for traction battery control software (battery shuts drive down to protect itself) and a separate AC compressor wiring fault that could shut the powertrain down. Owner reports on SpeakEV also describe intermittent traction faults traced to battery temperature sensor readings, and a fleet with 2024 vans reporting charge sessions stopping and drive cutting out (owner reports, unverified). Check for stored fault codes and confirm recall software is done.

knownIssues.issue: Flat 12V battery after standing (owner reports)
knownIssues.detail: Owners report Stellantis vans that won't start after standing (one 75kWh Vivaro after about six months), and 12V batteries not fully charged leading to recurring faults. Ex-fleet vans that sat in compounds are most at risk. Test or replace the 12V battery.

knownIssues.issue: Slow rapid charging in cold weather
knownIssues.detail: No battery preconditioning is documented, so DC rates fall when the pack is cold (a third-party troubleshooting guide cites below about 10-15C). Real average 10-80% on the 75kWh is about 77kW even in good conditions (EV Database). Plan on 45+ min stops in winter.

recalls.issue: AC compressor stator wiring can leak current and shut the powertrain down while driving; fix is ECU software reprogramming. Peugeot UK ref R/2023/140 (May 2023, 29,537 Peugeot EVs incl. e-Expert, e-Partner). A Vauxhall Vivaro-e/Combo-e 'powertrain shutdown' recall dated 8 May 2023 is listed by third-party trackers. Citroën/Toyota/Fiat equivalents not confirmed.
recalls.years: e-Expert builds approx 10/03/2020-07/12/2022 (third-party source; check VIN)

recalls.issue: Traction battery control unit software calibration could misread cell voltage/temperature and cut drive (loss of propulsion). Fix: software update. Stellantis/Toyota campaign announced March 2023 for 2022 builds; Toyota later issued CI25-007 for Proace BEV built 11 Jul 2022-21 Feb 2023.
Traction battery software recall listed for Vivaro (third-party tracker ref R/2025/119, March 2025). Not verified on DVSA; check VIN.

usedPrices: Approximate. Parkers' used-price guide (October 2026): £4,325-£29,500 (its range spans all ages, mileages and versions, and Parkers doesn't say what basis it uses). Dealer asking prices on Parkers (64 vans, 28 Oct 2026, nearly all + VAT): 2020-21 75kWh about £10,000-£10,700 + VAT at 50,000-68,000 miles; 2022 vans about £10,000-£14,000 + VAT (50 or 75kWh); 2023 75kWh about £12,100-£14,000 + VAT; 2024 facelift 75kWh about £14,200-£15,900 + VAT; 2025 50kWh about £14,400-£18,000 + VAT. A few 57,000-80,000-mile vans are listed at about £10,000 with no VAT. Trade values are lower: an October 2026 auction report had a 27k-mile 75kWh van stall at £9,900 + VAT. Asking prices, not sold prices.
bestBuy: A 2021-23 75kWh van, ideally with the 11kW charger if you have three-phase. Ex-lease examples with full dealer history and recalls done are the safest. A 2024-on facelift (217-mile WLTP) is worth the extra if budget allows.
avoid: 50kWh vans if you regularly do more than about 90-100 miles a day or tow/carry heavy loads in winter. Avoid any van with unresolved traction-fault warnings or no proof of recall work.
checks: Confirm battery size from the V5C/VIN or the dealer system, not the badge: there's no outside badge for 50 vs 75kWh, and adverts may say 49, 50 or 75kWh.
Check whether it has the optional 11kW three-phase onboard charger (advert/spec shows '11kW Charger' or '[11kWCh]'). Only matters if you have three-phase at the depot.
Run the VIN on the DVSA checker and ask a franchised dealer to confirm the 2023 traction-battery software and AC-compressor recall work is done (2020-22 builds especially).
Ask for a dealer battery health/state-of-health printout. Warranty cover is to 70% capacity, so you want the figure in writing.
Vauxhall vans are badge twins of the Expert/Dispatch: a Peugeot/Citroën dealer cannot do Vauxhall warranty work, so check your nearest Vauxhall commercial dealer.
confidence: medium-high. Battery sizes, WLTP figures, charging and warranty terms are now confirmed by Parkers. Least certain: the exact recall list (DVSA pages weren't reachable), usable battery figures (EV Database/GreenCarsCompare only) and the WLTP range of the facelift 50kWh van.
